name: Datum Atlas
tagline: A materials workbench: referenced materials data, property charts and selection, eco audit, process selection and microstructures, in one app for Windows.
for: Design and materials engineers, and students.
about: Datum Atlas is a materials workbench: modules that share one library of referenced materials. Library holds every material with its sources; Select puts them on property charts, where a design goal such as a light, stiff beam sets the chart, the selection line and the limits; Eco adds up energy and CO₂ through a product's life; Make finds the processes that can make the part and what it costs; Microstructure shows the typical structure of every class of material and measures your micrographs and generates synthetic grain structures; Crystal has the elements on a periodic table, compositions, and crystal calculators from spacings to X-ray patterns; EBSD opens orientation maps; DIC turns displacement fields into strain maps and links them to EBSD grains; Testing turns your tensile, hardness, fatigue and creep data into results and into a material of your own.

Every material is a bubble spanning its range of values. Limits, index lines, bands, boxes and shapes narrow the field; the materials that pass are ranked, and every one that fails says why. Compare the best, print a report, and add, import and share your own materials. corrosion and heat treatment modules are on the way.

steps.title: Pick a goal
steps.text: Choose a design goal, or set the two properties to chart yourself.

steps.title: Chart and select
steps.text: Move the selection line, add limits and boxes, and watch the field narrow.

steps.title: Rank, check and report
steps.text: See the materials that pass, ranked. Compare the best, audit their energy and CO₂, choose how to make the part, and print the selection report.

highlights: About 250 materials from every family, compiled from open and public sources. Every value names its source; 73 values are checked against published datasheets so far, and gaps stay gaps, never zero.
Property charts of any two properties or of your own formulas, with family envelopes, the best materials labelled and labels kept apart; bar charts; up to four charts side by side.

25 design goals and a library of 52 performance indices, including low-carbon and low-energy ones, with an index builder; a goal sets the axes, the selection line and the limits in one pick, and explains why.
Selection by limits, index lines, bands, boxes, drawn shapes and families; results ranked by an index or by weighted properties, with the reason every other material fails.

An eco audit: energy and CO₂ of a product from its materials to the end of its life, for up to four design options, with the largest phase named, the break-even life, and greener substitutes for the same job.
Process selection from 55 processes: the ones that can make your part from your material, why the others cannot, and the cost per part against batch size; joins and finishes that suit it.

Compare up to six materials with a radar chart, and print a selection report with the charts, shortlist, eco audit, manufacture and datasheets. Your own materials and databases, spreadsheet and CSV import and export, SI or imperial units.
A command line beside the app, and a connection for AI assistants (Model Context Protocol): search materials, read datasheets with their sources, run a selection, the eco audit and process selection.
A guide of about thirty pages with numbered pictures, in the app and on every release page.
Modules sharing one library: Library, Select, Eco, Make, Microstructure and Crystal, with a switcher.
The 118 elements on a periodic table, compositions in weight and atom percent, and crystal calculators: spacings, angles, X-ray powder patterns and stereographic projections.
Testing: tensile results with statistics, hardness statistics, S–N curves with Basquin's law and creep rupture on a Larson–Miller plot; the results become a material of your own.
Image analysis of micrographs: calibrate from the scale bar, then phase fraction, porosity, particles, grain size with G, graphite nodularity and coating thickness.
A structure generator: synthetic grain maps with the size, spread, elongation, second phase, pores and texture you choose, coloured by orientation, measured back and ready for image analysis.
EBSD: open .ang and .ctf maps; orientation, phase and quality maps; grains, boundaries, Σ3 twins, local misorientation, Schmid factors, pole figures and inverse pole figures.
DIC: strain maps from displacement fields, with statistics and profiles, and strain by grain linked to an EBSD map, with Schmid factors and slip traces.

roadmap.title: Corrosion
items: Galvanic compatibility, resistance by environment, corrosion allowance.

roadmap.title: Heat treatment and phase diagrams
items: Hardenability, tempering, welding preheat; binary phase diagrams with the lever rule.

roadmap.title: Stable
items: About 1,000 materials with pictures and microstructures, and a signed installer.
